_readme: LEVEL 2 GUIDE: same format as Tutorials/Level_01/guide.json (see its _readme, _targets and _triggers, and Documentation/LevelGuideTutorial/README.md).

Level 2 assumes Level 1's basics (moving, the HUD, filling folder fields from the book) and teaches what is new: the Taxpayer Profile, the Findings slip, the stamps, the toolkit colours, the annotated papers and the Reviewed Schedule.
No arrows inside the office (the player knows it). Only Rosa's stall, a new place, gets arrows (revealArrows is not needed: trail.waitForGuide is off).

Level 2 triggers: cue:<name> (GameplayEvents.RaiseGuideCue: FindingsPaperLifted, FindingsPaperFiled, StampsUp, TaxBookStored, AnnotatedPapersOpened, AnnotatedPapersStacked, AnnotatedPapersPutAway, ScheduleLineFilled, OfficeConclusionSet) and flag:<name> (Level2OfficeStart.Flag: inFileRoom, folderRetrieved, bookStored, initialStamped, recordsCollected, questDone, officeReview).
Arthur points to book sections by number (Sections 1-3 shared, 4-9 in Levels/Level_02/book.json); keep the numbers in step with the book.
The guide only observes: it never changes the case, the review phase, rewards or documents.
Fields starting with '_' are notes and are ignored by the game.

welcome.title: Something Does Not Match
welcome.subtitle: ONE MARKET CLIENT · ONE PREPARED SUMMARY
welcome.tagline: Check Aling Rosa's income summary against the records behind it.

_waypoints: Arrows only lead to places new in Level 2: the file storage room (first visit, until the folder is taken), Rosa's stall and her records desk. Familiar office steps (receptionist, desk, Auditor) have no waypoint.

pages.text: Welcome back! Today you have one client: Aling Rosa, who runs a laundry shop at the market.
Someone already filled in her income summary. Your job is to check it, not just accept it.
You know the office by now. Start at the front desk: the receptionist has your assignment.
You haven't been to the file storage room yet. Follow the glowing line on the floor.
This is the file storage room. Every client the office helps has a folder in one of these cabinets.
The cabinets are sorted by client group, and each drawer has a label card. Rosa is a market vendor, so her folder sits in the MARKET CLIENTS drawer.
Get in the habit of reading the label before you open a drawer. Taking the wrong client's folder is a real mistake in this job.
Your turn: walk up to the MARKET CLIENTS drawer and tap it to take Rosa's folder.
Got it! Rosa's folder is in your Case Folder icon. Go to your desk in the consultant office and sit down.
Your turn: tap your Case Folder icon. Rosa's folder lands on the desk and opens.
Page 1 is Taxpayer Information, just like last time: Classification, Type and Income Source are empty.
There's no profile card for Rosa. Instead, turn one page: her Taxpayer Profile describes her in a single sentence.
Read it slowly. Is she Filipino? Where does she live? Does someone employ her, or does she run her own work? Who pays her, and for what?
Then match each answer to the Tax Code Book: Section 1 for Classification, Section 2 for Type, Section 3 for Income Source.
You did this in Level 1, so it's your turn now. Profile, book, folder!
Read the Taxpayer Profile, then fill Classification, Type and Income Source on page 1 from Sections 1 to 3.
Nicely done. Now the real work of Level 2: checking someone else's numbers.
Turn to the Summary page. The Assistance Desk listed Rosa's May income there: clothes washing, washer rental, and a May total.
Then read the Payment Note on the next page. It mentions a job Rosa was paid for in May.
Here's the question: is the money from that job anywhere in the Summary? Check every line, and the total.
When two papers don't agree, we write it down on the Findings page. The paper taped there is your Findings slip.
Your turn: turn to the Findings page and tap the slip, or drag it, to lift it off the page.
It's loose now. Drag it anywhere on the desk while you work: it stays where you leave it, and the folder pages still turn underneath.
The slip has three boxes. ENTRY TO CHECK is the Summary line that may be wrong.
CLUE is the line on another paper that makes you doubt it. Clues come from the Payment Note.
REASON says why it's a problem. Reasons are in the Tax Code Book, Section 7, Finding Reasons. Read what each one means before you choose.
Fill a box like a folder field: tap a line, then tap the box. Or drag the line straight in.
Tip: think about which Summary line should hold every May payment, and which paper shows a payment it may have missed.
Fill Entry to check, Clue and Reason. When they point at the same problem, the slip writes a note.
That's a supported finding! See the handwritten note? The records raise a question we can't settle from the office.
Your turn: drag the Findings slip back onto the open folder. The folder turns to its page and the slip settles in.
One more thing before we visit Rosa. Every folder we hold gets an initial review stamp, so the office knows where it stands.
Do you see that stamp set on your desk? It has two stamps: READY and NOT READY.
READY means every payment is supported. NOT READY means a question is still open, like the one your finding just raised.
Your turn: tap the stamp set. The folder turns to its front page and both stamps rise beside it.
Now drag the stamp that fits onto the front page. A see-through ghost shows exactly where the ink will land.
Drag your stamp onto the folder's front page and let go over the ghost.
Recorded! Now we need the original receipt for that payment, and Rosa has it.
You'll want the Tax Code Book out there. If it's still on the desk, drag it onto the red book icon so it travels with you.
Tap Exit Desk to stand up when you're ready.
Rosa's stall is near the plaza. It's new to you, so follow the arrows outside and talk to her.
Rosa gave you four supporting records. Sit at her records desk beside the stall to begin Mark the Money!
Before you try, a quick guide to the colours in the toolkit.
The YELLOW highlighter marks the money line: the amount, and what it was paid for.
BLUE cards are TYPE: what kind of money it is. Pay from an employer, payment from customers, rent, interest, or a loan.
ORANGE cards are TREATMENT: what we do with it. The regular income schedule, a separate rule, an exclusion, or not income at all.
PURPLE tags are RECORD: the one paper that proves this payment. Clip the record written for it.
Stuck on a card? Open your Tax Code Book from its red icon. Section 4 explains every blue card, Section 5 every orange card, and Section 6 says which record counts.
Tap the yellow highlighter, drag it onto the salary line and sweep across. Add a blue TYPE card and an orange TREATMENT card, then clip the purple payslip tag.
Practice done! Now Rosa's four real records. This part is scored: your FIRST check decides your medal.
Use the tabs to switch records. On each one: highlight the money line, add one blue TYPE, one orange TREATMENT, and clip one purple RECORD.
Read every line before you choose. Who paid? For what? Does it have to be paid back? Those answers decide the colours.
No rush, and the book is allowed: Section 4 for blue, Section 5 for orange, Section 6 for records. Press CHECK when all four are marked.
Mark all four records, then press CHECK. Book: Section 4 blue, Section 5 orange, Section 6 records.
Your medal is set by that first check, so relax: nothing from here on changes it.
Green notes are right and locked in. Red notes need another look. Tap a red note and I'll give you a hint.
Swap the red notes, then CHECK again until every note is green.
Look at that: your four annotated papers went into the new icon on the right.
Each one keeps the money line you highlighted and the cards you placed. Back at the office, they ARE your evidence.
Your turn: tap the icon to spread them out.
To put them away, press and hold any paper for two seconds. Keep your finger still until they stack up under it.
Now drag the stack onto the icon and let go. Let go anywhere else and they just spread out again.
Perfect. Now take what you learned back to the office. Rosa's folder has new pages waiting at your desk.
Head back to your desk in the consultant office and sit down.
Welcome back. Now we fix Rosa's numbers properly.
Your turn: open Rosa's folder. Tap its icon, or drag it toward you if it is on the desk.
After Findings there's a new page: the Reviewed Schedule. It's Rosa's corrected May income, written by you.
It has two Summary lines, one Missing entry, the totals, and a Conclusion box below them.
Every amount comes from your annotated papers, never from the old Summary. Checking it is the whole point!
Two rules: each earned payment goes in once, and money that must be paid back stays out. Section 6 of your book explains both.
Your turn: tap an empty line. Your annotated papers spread out. Tap a highlighted amount, then tap the line. Dragging works too.
That's one line! Fill the others the same way. Which paper is the job the Summary forgot? That one is your Missing entry.
Last, the Conclusion box. It says what you did about your finding. Take it from Section 8, Review Conclusions.
Fill the two Summary lines, the Missing entry and the Conclusion. Stuck? Sections 6 and 8 of your book.
Your schedule is complete. Turn to the last page, Final Assessment: your work is summed up there in handwriting.
Read it like the Auditor will. Is every earned payment there, once? Is the loan kept out? Does the conclusion say what you did?
Section 9 of your book explains READY and NOT READY. Be honest: the Auditor checks it.
Same stamps as before. Your turn: tap the stamp set.
Drag your stamp onto the Final Assessment page.
Stamped! Put the folder in its icon, then take it to the Auditor's office. You know the way.
Hand Rosa's folder to the Auditor. If he returns it, fix only what he points to, stamp again and bring it back.
He sent it back, and that's okay: your work is all still in the folder.
Read his note again. It names the page and the book section to check. Fix only that, read the new summary on Final Assessment, stamp again, then bring it back.
